# function: flatten_nested_map

Return a single-level map with one element for each entry of each nested map in the input. Each result key is the parent key and the nested key joined by `.`. Each result element is an object with the attributes `parent_key`, `child_key`, and `child` (the nested entry). Attributes of the parent object can be retrieved by indexing the input with `parent_key`. This function replaces the standard nested map flattening algorithm (`flatten` with nested `for` expressions and `tomap`) for use with the `for_each` meta-parameter.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example is related to common design pattern algorithm described at https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/functions/flatten#flattening-nested-structures-for-for_each
# The below example demonstrates how to perform the above transformation in a very compact and clean function invocation as opposed to the obfuscated and messy standard approach described in the above documentation link.

# Flatten a nested map into a flat map:
resource "aws_subnet" "example" {
  for_each = provider::stdlib::flatten_nested_map(var.networks, "subnets")

  vpc_id            = aws_vpc.example[each.value.parent_key].id
  availability_zone = each.value.child_key
  cidr_block        = each.value.child.cidr_block
}
# result => {
#   "<parent_key>.<child_key>" = {
#     parent_key = "<parent_key>",
#     child_key  = "<child_key>",
#     child      = { cidr_block = "<cidr_block>" }
#   }
# }
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
flatten_nested_map(input dynamic, children_attribute string) dynamic
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `input` (Dynamic) Input map (or object) of objects to flatten. Each object must contain the nested map (or object) attribute named by the `children_attribute` parameter.
1. `children_attribute` (String) Name of the attribute in each input object that contains the nested map to flatten.
